name: Uniqode
summary: Dynamic QR codes and digital business cards with real-time scan analytics, to connect offline touchpoints to measurable results and capture leads.
best_for: marketing teams that need dynamic QR codes with real analytics and enterprise compliance (SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001, optional HIPAA)
skip_if: you only need the occasional QR code and do not need scan data: Uniqode has no free plan, so a free generator is a better fit, and Bitly is better if link-shortening is your main job
honest_knock: The tier jumps are steep and a lot is gated: analytics are capped at 30 days on the entry plan, only the first three plans have fixed prices, a second user means $99 a month, and reaching a plan's scan limit stops your dynamic codes. It's a real QR platform, but overkill if you just want the occasional code.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-11-18 on their own pricing page, plain HTML) The page now shows four plans. Essential $9 USD a month, billed yearly: 1 user, 30 days of scan analytics, 15 dynamic QR codes, 5 Linkpages. Core $49 a month, billed yearly: 1 user, 90 days of analytics, 250 dynamic codes, 10 Linkpages, the Una AI assistant. Plus $99 a month, billed yearly: 3 users, 180 days of analytics, 500 dynamic codes, 25 Linkpages, Una AI and a custom domain. Business+ is custom priced through sales and adds SSO, multi-org, 2-year analytics and pay by invoice. The comparison table lists annual scan allowances of 50,000, 1,000,000 and 2,000,000 for the first three plans. The page offers a 14-day free trial without a credit card, a 30-day money-back guarantee and no free plan: Uniqode confirmed to us by mail on 18 November 2026 that it has no free lifetime plan, and an earlier version of this review wrongly said static codes were free and unlimited. Per its FAQ, static codes you already made keep working after you cancel but you cannot create new ones, and dynamic codes stop working when the subscription ends or when you reach the scan limit. Our earlier figures for a $2,000-a-year custom domain add-on and $6-a-seat business cards are not on the page any more, so we no longer quote them.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 2 November 2026 on the free trial: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We created two dynamic website QR codes, exported the list to CSV, downloaded a QR image and read the analytics page. We did not open the checkout.
findings: The sidebar counted the 14-day trial down ('Your QR Codes will expire in 13d : 23hr : 58m') and warned that the codes expire when the trial ends: something to plan for before you print anything.

The analytics page showed 1,800 total scans and 1,296 unique scanners on a brand-new account, under the banner 'You're exploring a preview of your future insights'. These are sample figures; our CSV export showed 0 real scans for both codes.
The note field took one line; the second line of our note was lost while typing, and the saved note did not appear in the CSV export.
'Add to Watchlist' was switched on by default for each new code, with a promise of a daily scan notification.
The CSV export kept both QR IDs, destinations and names, including the Unicode characters in our second title. Bulk Upload carried a paid-plan crown, so we did not test bringing the file back in.
not_tested: Checkout, tax and the price after the trial
Bulk Upload and re-importing the CSV
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
